skill.name: styling-with-shadcn
skill.description: Build accessible Next.js interfaces with shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI patterns, form validation, tables, dialogs, sidebars, and dark mode.
skill.summary: Create polished shadcn/ui interfaces for Next.js applications.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, TSX template literals, and ordinary UI comments. The remaining confirmed issues are expected setup or verification commands and a Google Fonts import, which are legitimate but should be disclosed because they execute external tooling or contact a third-party service.

remediation.issue: External package setup commands use latest npm tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Pin shadcn CLI versions where possible and tell users to review generated changes before applying them.

remediation.issue: The theme example imports fonts from Google Fonts.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a self-hosted font option or disclose that the CSS import makes third-party network requests.

remediation.issue: The verification section asks users to run a local script.
remediation.suggestion: Explain what the verifier checks before asking users to run python3 scripts/verify.py.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent React interfaces without rebuilding component patterns from scratch. This skill provides practical shadcn/ui guidance for accessible Next.js forms, dialogs, tables, sidebars, themes, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Shows shadcn/ui setup commands for Next.js projects.
Provides component patterns for buttons, cards, dialogs, alert dialogs, tables, sidebars, and toasts.
Demonstrates react-hook-form and Zod validation with shadcn form components.
Includes dark mode setup using next-themes.
Provides theme and layout examples for a TaskFlow-style dashboard.
Lists related dependencies used by the examples.
limitations: Focused on React and Next.js applications only.
Does not replace current shadcn/ui documentation for version-specific changes.
Requires users to install and maintain project dependencies.
Examples may need adaptation for existing design systems.

use_cases.title: Create a validated product form
use_cases.description: Build a shadcn/ui form with inputs, select fields, textarea content, react-hook-form state, and Zod validation.

use_cases.title: Design an application dashboard
use_cases.description: Assemble cards, badges, data tables, sidebar navigation, and theme tokens into a cohesive dashboard interface.

use_cases.title: Add accessible interaction patterns
use_cases.description: Use dialogs, alert dialogs, loading buttons, toast feedback, and keyboard-friendly Radix-based components.

prompt_templates.title: Add a basic component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single UI element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use styling-with-shadcn to add a primary button and card layout to my Next.js page.

prompt_templates.title: Build a validated form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use styling-with-shadcn to create a task form with title, description, priority, react-hook-form, and Zod validation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a dashboard screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced layout with several component types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use styling-with-shadcn to design a dashboard with a sidebar, summary cards, status badges, and a data table.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a production UI flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that combines accessibility and UX states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use styling-with-shadcn to improve this Next.js workflow with dialogs, destructive confirmations, toast feedback, loading states, and dark mode support.

output_examples.input: Create a task form with validation.
output_examples.output: A plan for a shadcn form using Input, Textarea, Select, FormMessage, react-hook-form state, and a Zod schema.
A UI flow that uses AlertDialog for confirmation and Sonner toast messages for success and failure states.

best_practices: Install only the shadcn/ui components that the page needs.
Use Zod schemas and FormMessage components for clear validation feedback.
Keep dark mode tokens and component variants consistent across screens.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for non-React or non-Next.js projects.
Do not paste every component example into production without pruning unused code.
Do not bypass accessibility behavior provided by Radix-based shadcn/ui components.

faq.question: Does this skill install shadcn/ui automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and patterns, but the user or agent must choose when to run setup commands.

faq.question: Can it help with forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes react-hook-form, Zod validation, shadcn form components, messages, selects, and text areas.

faq.question: Does it cover dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows next-themes setup, a theme provider pattern, and a theme toggle approach.

faq.question: Is it suitable for existing design systems?
faq.answer: Yes, but examples should be adapted to match existing tokens, spacing, and component rules.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review external setup commands, dependency versions, and any third-party font imports before applying changes.
